findings.evidence: `FiniteTypeBaseChange.lean:116` fixes `A : CommAlgCat.{max w v} K` and `:152` fixes `B` likewise; `BaseChangeNaturality.lean:54`/`:61` impose the same restriction on `restrictScalars`. But `PointsFunctor.lean:48-54` has independent universes `{H : Type v}` and `(A : CommAlgCat.{w} R)`, returning `GrpCat.{max v w}`.
findings.fix: Introduce a separate universe, e.g. `universe u v w x`; generalize `CommAlgCat.restrictScalars`/`restrictScalarsMap` to `CommAlgCat.{x} K`, then state the equivalence and value/domain naturality for `A B : CommAlgCat.{x} K`.
findings.issue: `baseChangePointsMulEquiv` and its naturality lemmas only work for `A B : CommAlgCat.{max w v} K`, although points are naturally evaluated on `CommAlgCat.{x} K` for an independent universe.

summary: The finite-type base-change API unnecessarily ties the value-algebra universe to the coordinate/base-change universes. The natural points API already allows an independent value universe, so this wrapper should preserve that generality.
